description:
Mission Statement: Protecting Human Potential Beyond Earth.
We are building the next generation of spaceflight telemetry and biomedical software designed to monitor, analyze, and safeguard astronaut health in real time. Operating in extreme microgravity and deep-space radiation environments presents unique physiological risks—from muscle atrophy and neuro-vestibular shifts to cardiovascular deconditioning.
summary:
Orbitcare is an offline-first health monitoring and early-warning app for astronauts on long missions, built for a NASA-themed challenge. On trips to the Moon or Mars, messages to Earth are delayed and rescue is impossible, so astronauts must check their own health. NASA’s five hazards (radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, gravity fields, closed environments) affect the body, and the app helps astronauts understand results and act on them.

It records heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, respiration, temperature, glucose, sleep, mood, stress and cabin radiation. An explainable rules engine compares readings with configurable limits and each astronaut’s own baseline, spots trends, and shows green, amber or red status with the reason and next step, including when to contact the flight surgeon. It never diagnoses or prescribes. Other features include a clickable body map, trend charts, a data simulator, hazard education, emergency protocols, a ground control view and daily tasks with badges.

The design is mobile and tablet first, in white and pastel blue, with large glove-friendly buttons and status shown by color, icon and text. The stack is React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind, Recharts, FastAPI and SQLite, shared as an installable PWA link.
details: ORBITCARE is a spaceflight health-monitoring interface for astronaut self-assessment and ground mission-control review. It tracks health trends, explains NASA Human Research Program hazards, and flags records for medical review without diagnosing or prescribing. It runs in demo mode with simulated data, and can connect to Supabase for authenticated records.
